text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x) ::: x has siblings who are the same age.
ComplainOften(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopStrongBonds(x) ::: x develops strong bonds with their family members.

Premises:
∀x ((Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x)) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAgeSiblings(x) → (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x))) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (ComplainOften(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopStrongBonds(x)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
(Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∧ DevelopStrongBonds(luke) ⊕ ¬((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∨ DevelopStrongBonds(luke)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.

Conclusion:
ComplainOften(luke) ::: Luke complains often about annoying siblings.
